position.summary: The text describes France juggling at least four simultaneous pressures in late September 2026. Pope Leo XIV was in the final days of his visit to Lourdes and Metz, drawing large crowds and intense media attention. The Lecornu government was defending a budget plan of roughly 54 billion euros in cuts against a national debt approaching 120 percent of GDP, with the 10-year OAT yield pressing above 4.5 percent. First-wave protests against the police licence-to-kill bill had already taken place, and a second round was imminent. Macron had announced that France would send troops and defence systems to protect the Yanbu port and the Red Sea oil route. Iran had closed a French language centre in Tehran, and France was preparing to summon Iran's ambassador. Estonia and other EU states were complaining about France's role in easing sanctions on Alisher Usmanov. Fuel prices sat at record highs, heat waves pressured the nuclear grid, and the Goncourt prize had removed a novel over AI-use accusations. Zidane had held his first training session, and Mbappe dominated the football narrative.
